answer: A quartz-clear ledger can resist fake identities if every new agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact, with the stake slashed when peers prove fraud. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands means locking real value behind each one, so a Sybil swarm reaches its nadir of profitability fast: the attacker pays per identity while honest agents recover their stake. Like onyx, the record is hard and public, so a slashed identity cannot quietly return.
